title: Introduce peered private endpoint rotation with staged DNS fallback
author: Ava Thompson
release_notes: Adds a controlled, rollback-capable rotation operator for peered private control plane endpoints; staged DNS fallback ensures client stability during ENI/peering swaps. No user API changes; operator enabled behind feature-flag.
description:
Summary: This PR implements an automated, safety-first rotation and failover procedure for private control-plane endpoints that are reachable via VPC peering and ephemeral ENIs. Motivation: recent customer incidents showed that large-scale peering or ENI updates can cause client-side DNS cache exposure and traffic blackholing. The reconciler provides a staged plan: preflight, canary swap (single AZ), DNS TTL-targeted fallback, full rotation, and automated rollback on health regressions.

Design & key behaviors: 1) Introduces a new controller 'endpoint-rotator' (operator) that models rotations as a state machine (PREPARE -> CANARY -> PROMOTE -> VERIFY -> COMPLETE/ROLLBACK). All transitions are guarded by health and probe checks reported to the controlplane. 2) DNS strategy: when swapping ENIs/peering, the operator can optionally lower Route53 TTLs, create a short-lived CNAME-based fallback (staged-fallback.<cluster>), and only switch authoritative records after green checks. 3) Peering and ENI orchestration: operator sequences peering acceptance, route table warmup, ephemeral ENI attachment with strict security group staging, and explicit route propagation checks. 4) Feature flags: the operator is opt-in by cluster annotation (installer sets to off by default). 5) Safety nets: preflight + dry-run mode, per-cluster concurrency limits, and automatic rollback with delta snapshot for debugging.

What this PR changes (high-level): - terraform/ modules: updated controlplane endpoint module to emit rotation metadata and optional Route53 helper records - helm: adds endpoint-rotator chart with RBAC, metrics, and feature flag config - installer: wiring for enabling the rotator and migration job for existing endpoints - controller: new service code + unit tests + integration harness - e2e: staged smoke tests to validate canary transition and DNS fallback - docs: short runbook and upgrade notes

Migration notes & rollout plan: - Default remains unchanged; operator disabled until explicitly enabled by the installer. - Recommended rollout: enable in a single non-critical region, perform dry-run, then test canary on a staging cluster, then enable gradual rollouts per region. - If DNS providers do not support low TTLs, the operator will fall back to header-based grace periods and will surface a warning in the console.

Testing & validations: automated unit tests for state machine, integration tests exercising route propagation, and CI e2e that ran against a small simulated cross-account peering environment. Manual canary executed in sandbox with two AZs; health checks triggered expected rollback on synthetic failure.

Security & compliance: RBAC scoped to installer namespace; new IAM role for route53/peering actions documented; SG staging ensures no open ingress during transitional states. Security review completed by Priya Desai.

CI & merge: all pipeline stages passed after a flaky networking test was re-run. Merge method: squash and merge.

Related Linear/Jira: ENG-2045 (endpoint rotation operator), ENG-2071 (installer wiring), SUP-7891 (customer incident follow-up).
